To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the teacher-determined design of Internet-based lessons has proven most successful in terms of pedagogical soundness.

• teacher-determined lessons are most effective when the teacher has a high degree of technological expertise, when the lesson is designed for low-proficiency learners, and when the lesson is limited in its scope. • teacher-facilitator lessons are most effective for high proficiency learners, for lessons that include multiple resources, and for lessons that require a high degree of learner involvement in determining what they will learn and how they will learn. • student-centered lessons are most effective in a high technology environment, when the

• the teacher-centered approach is best suited for students who have low language proficiency and little technological experience, and for teachers who have limited technological expertise; • the teacher-facilitator approach is best suited when the teacher has some technological expertise, and when the students are more advanced in their language proficiency and technological experience. • the learner-centered approach is best for teachers with a lot of technological expertise and for students with a high language proficiency and technological expertise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: What is the optimal approach to integrating Internet-based materials into a foreign-language curriculum?
the question of whether and how the Internet can be integrated into a foreign language classroom in a pedagogically sound way.
the following questions: What are the different ways of designing Internet-based reading materials for foreign language learning?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the teacher-centered approach is best suited for the initial stages of the learning process.

the more teacher-determined an approach, the more control a teacher has over the learning resources and tasks, the less technological expertise is required, and the more teacher-student interaction takes place.

the most successful approach is a combination of all three approaches, depending on the learners' proficiency level, the teacher's technological and pedagogical skills, as well as the learning objectives and content of the lesson.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the teacher-facilitator approach is the most promising approach for the design of Internet-based reading material lessons in a foreign language classroom.
Internet-based reading materials are a promising and useful tool for language teachers and students alike.
Internetbased lessons are most successful when they are designed to fit the needs of the learners, their language proficiency and the technological expertise of the teacher.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the teacher's role in integrating Internet-based reading material into the curriculum can be either teacher-determined or facilitator-determined.
the teacher's role in the design and implementation of Internet-based lessons is crucial and should not be underestimated.

Internet-based reading materials are not only an exciting resource for the foreign language classroom, but they also allow teachers to design lessons that are more learner-centered and more closely reflect the students' interests and language proficiency level.
